topic_candidates.title: Who Gets Control When an AI Agent Uses Your Bank Account?
topic_candidates.query: Reuters October 22 2026 US banks blocking third-party AI agents customer accounts transactions
topic_candidates.brief: A plain-English explanation of why banks are blocking outside AI agents that log in for customers. The video follows the chain: a person gives an agent credentials, the agent browses like a user, and the bank must decide whether an action was authorised. It explains the engineering problem underneath: agents can plan and execute multi-step tasks, but banks cannot reliably tell whether each action came from the customer or from the model’s own interpretation.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Reuters reported on October 22, 2026 that major U.S. banks were blocking third-party agents from entering customer accounts or making transactions. The report said some customers had shared login details with agents, while banks were concerned about agents acting beyond user instructions; it did not establish that customer funds had been stolen. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/us-banks-are-blocking-third-party-ai-agents-access-to-customer-accounts-sources-say-ce785cdedc80f72d))
topic_candidates.broke_on: The breakout titled "US banks scramble to control their AI agent activity" at 46.5 hours old; the underlying Reuters report was published October 22, 2026.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Agentic AI, authentication, permissions, audit trails and the difference between predicting a next step and safely executing a financial transaction.

topic_candidates.title: How to Hide the IPhone Duo Crease…
topic_candidates.query: Apple iPhone Duo crease cover layer hinge folding screen AP October 2026
topic_candidates.brief: A visual explanation of why foldable screens show a crease and why it is not something users should try to repair with pressure or a third-party protector. The video explains that the inner display must repeatedly bend, while the hinge and protective cover layer manage stress and surface damage. It gives viewers the practical takeaway: the crease is a design trade-off, and dust or a damaged cover layer can matter more than the visible line itself.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Apple says the Duo uses a folding inner display, a precision hinge and a nano-texture finish intended to reduce crease visibility. The Associated Press reported that the inner screen has different protection requirements from a conventional phone and warned that folding-phone hinges can admit debris; it also reported a replaceable cover-layer detail while noting Apple had not publicly confirmed all care guidance. ([apple.com](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/))
topic_candidates.broke_on: The breakout titled "How to fix the IPhone Duo crease…" at 30.4 hours old.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Flexible OLED mechanics, repeated bending fatigue, hinge tolerances, protective films and particulate contamination.

topic_candidates.title: Are the iPhone Duo’s Cameras Really Different??
topic_candidates.query: Apple official iPhone Duo dual capture folding camera outer display 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Rather than repeating that the cameras are good or bad, this video explains what changes when a phone folds. The order is: show the outer and inner screens, demonstrate hands-free framing, then explain why the second display can let subjects see themselves or join a FaceTime shot. The engineering underneath is a combination of camera placement, dual-display coordination and software that keeps two video feeds synchronised.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Apple’s launch information says the Duo has a folding design with dual displays, Dual Capture for simultaneous front and rear feeds, and Duo FaceTime features that use the outer display so people can see or join the shot. These are documented capabilities, not a claim that the camera quality is universally better. ([apple.com](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/))
